title: Dedicated throughput & surge scenario matrix — quarterly roadmap
creator: Sana Gupta
description:
Problem statement: Customers with reserved dedicated pools have highly variable traffic patterns. We need a repeatable quarterly plan that defines throughput guarantees, surge lanes, fallback behavior, and cost trade-offs so sales and SRE can commit to SLAs without over-reserving capacity.

Goals:
- Produce a scenario matrix mapping expected traffic profiles to reserve commitments and autoscale guardrails.
- Define standardized commitment bands (e.g., baseline, buffer, surge) with clear cost and latency trade-offs.
- Deliver playbooks for canarying surge policies and automatic fallback to hosted variants.
- Ship a set of product OKRs and dashboard panels to measure adherence and regression detection.

Approach / scope:
- Quarter slice: start with 3 representative customer archetypes (chatbot high-RPS, batch-embedding periodic spikes, mixed low-latency + burst).
- For each archetype, model token throughput distribution, tail latency risk, and cost at three quantization and batching profiles.
- Build the scenario matrix (rows: archetypes; columns: baseline, +20% buffer, +burst lane) with recommended committed vGPU, prewarm strategy, and autoscale cooldowns.
- Produce a rollout plan for Dedicated customers: pilot with two early-access accounts, run a 4-week experiment, collect latency and cost metrics, then generalize.

Deliverables:
- Scenario matrix spreadsheet and decision rules (Confluence doc).
- Three product change PRDs: Guarantee bands, Surge lane UX for Console, and Billing/tier rules.
- Two engineering tickets for autoscale policy primitives and a prewarm API.
- Dashboard templates (Console) and Grafana panels for SLO/usage.
- Playbook for on-call and CSMs for when surges exceed planned bands.

Milestones (high level):
- 2026-02-28: Archetype definitions & data pulls complete.
- 2026-03-10: Initial scenario matrix draft; review with Eng and SRE.
- 2026-03-24: Pilot plan and PRDs reviewed by GTM and Legal.
- 2026-04-07: Engineering spin-up for autoscale primitives and prewarm API.
- 2026-04-15: Pilot launch.
- 2026-05-15: Pilot complete; analysis and decision to generalize.

Success criteria / OKRs:
- OKR 1: Reduce unplanned capacity-originated latency incidents for Dedicated customers by 40% for pilot accounts.
- OKR 2: Achieve <10% median cost uplift vs current unoptimized reservations while meeting a 95th percentile latency SLO for pilot traffic shapes.
- OKR 3: Ship Console surge lane UI and two dashboard templates by release date.

Acceptance criteria:
- Scenario matrix contains actionable commit suggestions for all three archetypes.
- Pilot demonstrates acceptable trade-offs (latency SLO met, cost within target band).
- PRDs approved and dependencies (ENG tickets) scheduled for development in the release.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Overly conservative commitment bands increase cost for customers; overly aggressive bands create SLA risk.
- Engineering work on autoscale primitives risks schedule slippage; fallback to hosted variants must be tested.
- Billing alignment and legal review for surge billing could delay GA.

Open questions:
- Should surge lanes bill pro-rata versus flat per-surge-unit pricing? (Finance & Sales input required)
- What minimum telemetry sample size do we need to model customer archetypes reliably?
- How to expose commitment tiers in self-serve Console without increasing sign-up friction?
